:::{#thm-collision-entropy-at-most-entropy}
#### The collision entropy is at most the Shannon entropy

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) with values $x_1, \ldots, x_n$.
Then the [collision entropy](#def-renyi-entropy) is at most the [entropy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#def-entropy):

$$\renyientropyf{2}{X} \le \entropyf{X}.$$

The two coincide exactly when each value that $X$ takes with positive [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) has the same probability.

:::

::: proof

Write $\Pf{X}$ for the [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) evaluated at $X$.
The function $-\log$ is [strictly convex](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-convex-function),
so [Jensen's inequality](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#thm-jensen) gives

$$\E{-\log \Pf{X}} \ge -\log \E{\Pf{X}},$$

with equality exactly when $\Pf{X}$ is constant.
The left side is $\entropyf{X}$.
The right side is $\renyientropyf{2}{X}$ by its definition.
The function $\Pf{X}$ is constant exactly when every value that $X$ takes with positive [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) has that same probability. <!-- check-term-links: allow -->

:::
